samples.summary: Every new HttpClient method (folders CRUD, copyDocument, moveDocument) is mocked away; no test exercises the real URL, verb or body they build
samples.evidence: `packages/cli/test/folders.test.ts:22-33` replaces the whole `HttpClient` class with a stub (`vi.mock('../src/client/http-client.js', () => ({ HttpClient: class { ... } }))`), so the assertions only prove the commander wiring calls a named method. The `--dry-run` assertions (e.g. line ~200 `url: `${BASE}/folders``) are built by `printDryRun` inside `commands/folders.ts`, an independent duplicate of the path — they never run `HttpClient.listFolders()` etc. Meanwhile `packages/cli/test/http-client-paths.test.ts`, the only suite that drives the real client against a stubbed `fetch`, was not extended for any of the seven new methods added in `packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:311-344`. Consequently a wrong path (`/folder` vs `/folders`), a wrong verb, or a wrong body key (e.g. `createFolder` emitting `parent` instead of `parentId`, which the server would silently ignore and file the folder at the root) ships with a fully green suite.
searchedFor: glob packages/cli/test/*.ts for any other client-level suite (http-client.test.ts, dry-run.test.ts, namespaces.test.ts reviewed via diff)

samples.summary: The `$transaction` mock hands back the same prisma mock as `tx`, so the atomicity the test's comment claims to prove is unobservable
samples.evidence: `createMockPrisma` defines `$transaction: jest.fn((fn) => fn(prisma))` (spec lines ~36-45) — the callback receives the outer mock, not a distinct transaction client. The new test then asserts `expect(prisma.apiKey.updateMany).toHaveBeenCalledWith(...)` and `expect(prisma.$transaction).toHaveBeenCalled()` under the comment "Both halves land together, so a key cannot survive a committed removal" (spec line ~338). That assertion holds identically if `workspace.service.ts` were rewritten to call `this.prisma.workspaceMember.delete(...)` / `this.prisma.apiKey.updateMany(...)` outside the transaction body — the classic escape-the-tx bug — because the mock cannot tell `tx` from `this.prisma`. The test proves the two calls happen and that `$transaction` was invoked at some point, not that the revocation is inside it.

samples.summary: No test that a cross-workspace `parentId` actually aborts folder creation — only that `assertSameWorkspace` was called
samples.evidence: `folders.controller.spec.ts:92-95` ("checks a supplied parent belongs to the route workspace") asserts nothing but `expect(folderService.assertSameWorkspace).toHaveBeenCalledWith('f-9', WS)`, with the mock resolving. There is no case where `assertSameWorkspace` rejects and `folderService.create` is asserted not to have been called — so a reordering that creates the folder first (or drops the `await` in `folders.controller.ts:94-96`) would still pass, letting a folder be nested under another workspace's folder. Contrast the document path, which does have such a case (`documents.controller.spec.ts:216 'refuses a folder from another workspace'`).
searchedFor: grep for assertSameWorkspace across backend src

samples.summary: `copy` has only happy-path coverage: no API-key caller, no failure case, nothing pinning the deliberate "membership only" gate
samples.evidence: The `describe('copy')` block (documents.controller.spec.ts:157-174) contains exactly two tests: a member copy and a lookup-scoping assertion. The handler's documented invariant — that copy is intentionally NOT manager-gated and that an API key may copy — has no test (`req(..., true)` is never used for copy), and nothing asserts the source lookup's `NotFoundException` propagates without touching `documentCopyService.copy`. If a later edit added a manager gate or dropped the workspace scoping on copy, only the second test would catch the latter.
searchedFor: grep for copyDocument/DocumentCopyService in backend specs

samples.summary: `folderId` on the document PATCH body is an inline type with no DTO validation, and no test covers a non-string value
samples.evidence: `documents.controller.ts:115` types the body inline (`{ title?: string; folderId?: string | null }`), so — as the spec's own comment at documents.controller.spec.ts:256-261 notes — the global `ValidationPipe({ whitelist: true })` strips and validates nothing here. The tests exercise only `'f-1'`, `null` and omission; no case sends a non-string `folderId` (object/number/array), which would flow into `folderService.assertSameWorkspace(...)` and `data.folder = { connect: { id: <object> } }`. The equivalent folder route is protected by `UpdateFolderDto`; the document route is not, and no test pins the difference.
searchedFor: grep for ValidationPipe configuration references in the spec comments

samples.summary: Folder `update` lacks the combined rename+move case and the empty-body case that the document spec has
samples.evidence: `documents.controller.spec.ts:245` covers 'renames and moves in one call'; the folder spec's `describe('update')` (folders.controller.spec.ts:151-217) has no equivalent, so nothing pins that `data` accumulates both `name` and `parentId`. There is also no case for a body with neither field, where `folders.controller.ts:138` still issues `folderService.update(folderId, {})`.

samples.summary: Part of the traversal test is vacuously true: the client is asserted uncalled on a `--dry-run` path where it is never reached anyway
samples.evidence: In 'refuses a traversing id before any request' the command is run as `['folders', 'delete', '..', '--dry-run']`, and `expect(deleteFolder).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` holds for every `--dry-run` invocation regardless of whether `seg()` refuses `..` — the dry-run branch returns before any client call. Only the `exitCode`/`error.command` assertions carry information. A non-dry-run variant would be needed to show the refusal blocks a real request.

samples.summary: `docs copy` / `docs move` have no traversal-id refusal test, unlike the sibling `folders delete`
samples.evidence: `commands/docs.ts` places the `seg(docId)` dry-run preview inside the `try` specifically so a `.`/`..` id surfaces through `outputError` (comment at the top of the copy action), but `packages/cli/test/folders.test.ts`'s `describe('docs copy and move')` block contains no case passing `..` as the doc id; only `folders delete` has one.
searchedFor: grep for "folders.delete" / error.command assertions in packages/cli/test

verdict.reason: Verified the absence claim. packages/cli/test/folders.test.ts:22-32 replaces the whole HttpClient class with a seven-method stub, so every behavioral assertion (lines 143, 151, 180, 201, 212, 249, 310, 330, 338) only proves commander calls a named method. The --dry-run assertions (126, 160, 189, 221, 258, 321, 347) are satisfied by printDryRun literals built inside packages/cli/src/commands/folders.ts:39, 60-63, 85-87, 114-116, 137 — an independent duplicate of the route that never invokes the client. I searched wide for a real-client counterexample: vitest.config.ts:5 scopes the suite to test/**/*.test.ts; of the 8 files there that construct a real HttpClient or stub fetch, http-client-paths.test.ts (read in full) exercises only getDocument/deleteDocument/getCell/getCells/listTabs/getDocContent/revokeApiKey/listApiKeys/listDocuments/uploadFileDocument, and http-client.test.ts (read in full) covers only api-key endpoints and 401 refresh; dry-run.test.ts:24 and read-dry-run.test.ts:43 also mock HttpClient. Repo-wide grep for listFolders/createFolder/renameFolder/moveFolder/deleteFolder/copyDocument/moveDocument surfaces no other CLI test (remaining hits are the frontend's own api/folders.ts client and backend supertest specs, which never touch the CLI client); namespaces.test.ts:168-191 and schema.test.ts:135-179 assert only command presence and registry safety, and src/schema/registry.ts carries no route/verb data, so no route-parity mechanism exists. Consequence: a wrong path, verb, or body key in http-client.ts:311-344 (e.g. createFolder emitting parent instead of parentId, which the backend reads as unspecified and files at the root) ships with a fully green suite — a silently data-misplacing, user-visible failure with no meaningful test, i.e. major under the missing-tests rubric.

searchedFor: grep '/folders' in packages/backend/test (only web routes found)

mergedFrom.summary: Folder `update` has no test that a rejected `assertSameWorkspace` blocks the write, and none combining name + parentId in one call

finding.summary: `create`'s cross-workspace parent check is only asserted by "the mock was called" — no test proves a rejected parent stops the folder being created
finding.evidence: The only coverage for the parent check in `create` is `it('checks a supplied parent belongs to the route workspace')`, which asserts `expect(folderService.assertSameWorkspace).toHaveBeenCalledWith('f-9', WS)` and nothing else. That assertion holds even if the controller dropped the `await` (or ignored a rejection), in which case a folder could be parented under a folder in another workspace. The sibling `documents.controller.spec.ts` does have the corresponding negative case ('refuses a folder from another workspace' → rejects and `updateDocument` not called); the folders spec has no equivalent for `create`: no test mocks `assertSameWorkspace.mockRejectedValue(...)` and asserts `folderService.create` was not called. The v1 folders routes also have no e2e coverage (packages/backend/test/folder.e2e-spec.ts only hits the web routes `/workspaces/:id/folders` and `/folders/:id`), so nothing else exercises this path.

verdict.reason: Verified directly. ApiV1FoldersController.create (folders.controller.ts:94-104) depends on the awaited assertSameWorkspace rejection to prevent folderService.create; the only test for it (folders.controller.spec.ts:92-95) asserts nothing but toHaveBeenCalledWith('f-9', WS), while the beforeEach mock (line 67) always resolves — so it passes even if the await were dropped or the rejection swallowed. Searched wide for a counterexample and found none: repo-wide, the only assertSameWorkspace.mockRejectedValue uses are documents.controller.spec.ts:217 and files.controller.spec.ts:265 (different controllers); all ApiV1FoldersController references are api-v1.module.ts:60, the write-scope metadata table api-key-write-scope.guard.spec.ts:69, and this spec; and no test under packages/backend/test hits /api/v1/workspaces/:wid/folders (folder.e2e-spec.ts:155-273 only exercises web routes /workspaces/:id/folders and /folders/:id). The same negative pattern is applied to update in the very same file (lines 192-199: assertNoCycle rejects, update not called) but never to create. This is the lens's explicit "only asserting a mock was called" case over a cross-workspace parent guard, so a silently weakened guard could ship undetected — in-lane and blocking.
